The intention is to ensure that avatars render with the correct head color instead of appearing black.

Now I need to verify that these changes actually have the desired visual effect. I also ran that script once before the patches and captured the screenshots (11-avatar-face.png and 12-ingame-face.png), but I haven’t inspected them yet because the tool didn’t return image data. Regardless, the crucial step now is to re‑run the script so that it generates fresh screenshots reflecting the updated rendering logic.

I don’t need to modify the script any further; it already points to the local server, creates a random user, and captures the avatar preview. The only thing left is to execute it and wait for it to finish (allowing enough time for the browser launch and screenshot). Therefore, the next logical action is to invoke a Bash command that runs `node /tmp/glint-face-check.js` with a reasonable timeout.

This will produce new screenshots that I can later read and examine to confirm the face is now rendered correctly (white background showing head color). Hence I will issue the tool call to run the script.
